The most general form of the integral goes all the way back to t=-inf, which corresponds to the entire life of the capacitor. The voltage appearing on the capacitor depends on the amount of charge on the capacitor (v=q/C). The amount of charge depends on the current that has flowed into and out of the capacitor over its lifetime (I = dq/dt). the t=-inf limit covers all that time between creation and t=0.
